sections.html: A fast-swimming cichlid from the lower Congo catchment area, growing up to 10 cm. It is generally regarded as the world's flattest cichlid. At first sight it looks like the better-known T. brichardi, but T. depressum, as its species name says, is distinctly more flattened, which is especially visible when it props itself on the ground with its belly fins in its typical way.
As the animals are territorial, despite their small size you should have an aquarium with a minimum capacity of 160 l.

Care hardly causes any problems for the keeper. Plants are not eaten and there are no special demands on the water values. Being cave breeders, they love cramped niches and clefts in which they can retire and later spawn. The tighter the cleft, the better they feel inside. Flat-lying stones are partly undermined by the animals themselves, creating holes.
Very easy to feed with all common foods.

The sexes can be distinguished rather easily. Females soon show a broad red-orange zone on the tail fin, which males do not have or which is reduced to a very small line. Females ready to spawn show a yellow-orange to reddish belly. Males keep the usual brown-black base colour.
Cave breeders; they retire into cramped niches and clefts and spawn their eggs there.
